column1: # Чем получено: the three RuleOptionKeyRecognition::FRAMEWORK_KEYS — where recognised,
#   grep -rn "<spelling>" src/ --include='*.php'        # run once per spelling, see counts below
#                                                     # calls a rule's analyze(); the other 3 hits are
#   find src -name '*Rule.php' | xargs grep -ln "extends AbstractRule" | wc -l        -> 36
#   find src -name '*Rule.php' | xargs grep -hn "const string NAME" | wc -l           -> 50
#   - Three spellings exist and they are NOT interchangeable at every seam: the dashed form
#     lives only in FRAMEWORK_KEYS, the snake_case form is the config-file/constant form,
#     the camelCase form is what a CLI key folds to. A fourth framing (e.g. a key inside a
#     YAML anchor, or a title-case form in a doc table) would be missed — the greps search
#   - Counts below are raw grep hits over src/*.php: they include docblock mentions and
#     constant declarations, not only live reads. They are a denominator, not an inventory
#     of effects. tests/, website/ and qmx.yaml were not counted.
#   - "How many rules execute them" is answered by tracing the registry getters to their
#     single caller. If some other consumer read the raw options array directly and
#     re-implemented the match, this trace would not show it. The one near-miss found —
#     ConfiguredSuppression — is listed: it re-reads the raw options, but only to NAME the
#     patterns that already fired, not to decide.
#   (each dashed form occurs exactly once: its entry in FRAMEWORK_KEYS)
#   No *Rule.php class reads any of the three keys. The effect is applied post hoc, once,
#   to every finding of every producer, in FindingExclusionLedger::keeps(), called from
